subject: variance accounted for by covariates in MQM

messages.author: 7a1a0c66d60b0f26
messages.subject: variance accounted for by covariates in MQM
parts:
I am building multiple QTL models for several traits and am including
covariate phenotypes for some traits. My question is what exactly the
variance attributed to the covariate represents in terms of potential
genetic variance attributable to both the trait being mapped and the
covariate. For instance, if mapping a phenotype with a strong
difference between sexes then one might expect that inclusion of sex
as a covariate will account (and thus remove) the effect of sex
determining loci in the model. Is this correct or are we in fact
potentially mapping sex determiners as well as QTL responsible for the
phenotype of interest?
Thanks
